questions.question:
D1.4 — E4 Telegram: include the Telegram bot API integration in this quarter's scope?
Project/branch/task: main branch; choosing 2-3 of 5 chat integrations for the quarter, one candidate at a time (4 of 5). E1 and E3 Included (2 of 3 slots used), E2 Deferred. One slot remains and E5 Mattermost is still to be asked.
ELI10: Telegram is the cheapest build at about a week with the simplest API, and it serves about 8% of asks, mostly international users. Your own plan calls it low strategic value. The catch is the last slot: if you include Telegram now, Mattermost (asked next) cannot be included without reopening this answer. Mattermost serves fewer people (3%) but every one of them is a high-ARR self-hosted enterprise account, which is a retention play rather than a volume play. Deferring Telegram keeps the slot open for that comparison and costs little, since a one-week build is easy to slot in whenever capacity frees up.
Stakes if we pick wrong: including it may lock Mattermost out of the quarter and spend the last slot on the lowest-strategic-value option; cutting it abandons a cheap win and the international segment for good.
Recommendation: B) Defer because it is the easiest candidate to fit in later, the plan rates it low strategic value, and the last slot should be weighed against the high-ARR Mattermost accounts first.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Include in this quarter's scope
  ✅ Cheapest win on the list: about one human week for 8% of asks, with the simplest API surface and lowest build risk.
  ✅ Serves international users who are otherwise unreached by Slack and Teams, broadening geographic coverage.
  ❌ Uses the last of three slots, so E5 Mattermost (high-ARR, self-hosted enterprise) cannot be included without revisiting this answer.
B) Defer to next quarter (TODOS.md) (recommended)
  ✅ Keeps the third slot open to weigh Mattermost's high-ARR retention value before the set is fixed.
  ✅ A one-week build is the easiest item to pull forward if a slot frees up mid-quarter, so deferral costs almost nothing.
  ❌ International users keep waiting, and a cheap, visible win is delayed for a segment that may feel overlooked.
C) Cut entirely
  ✅ Removes a low-strategic-value item from the roadmap for good and keeps the product story focused on business platforms.
  ✅ Avoids the ongoing maintenance of a fifth platform adapter that serves a small, non-core segment.
  ❌ Abandons 8% of asks and the international segment permanently for the sake of one week of work; poor trade on cost alone.
D) Hold — stop the chain and discuss first
  ✅ Lets you decide whether the cap is really 3 or whether a one-week item can sit outside it before committing.
  ✅ No disposition is recorded, so nothing has to be unwound.
  ❌ Stops the review here; E5 is not asked until you say continue.
Net: you are trading a cheap, low-strategic-value win now for keeping the last slot open to compare against high-ARR retention.

questions.question:
D1.5 — E5 Mattermost: include the Mattermost REST plugin in this quarter's scope?
Project/branch/task: main branch; choosing 2-3 of 5 chat integrations for the quarter, one candidate at a time (5 of 5, last). E1 and E3 Included (2 of 3 slots used), E2 and E4 Deferred. One slot remains.
ELI10: Mattermost is only 3% of asks, but every one of those asks comes from a high-ARR, self-hosted enterprise account. These are the exact buyers for an incident-alert product: DevOps teams running their own chat for compliance reasons, with Mattermost's own incident playbooks already in use. They are locked in to Mattermost, so if you do not meet them there, they do not switch chat tools, they switch vendors. The plan says 2 weeks, but Mattermost's incoming webhooks are Slack-compatible by design, so with Slack shipping first the real cost is likely closer to a week. This is the last slot, and including it brings the set to exactly the cap.
Stakes if we pick wrong: including it spends the last slot on the smallest user count; deferring leaves your highest-ARR accounts without a path to the feature their peers on Slack and Teams get this quarter.
Recommendation: A) Include because it protects the highest-ARR accounts at the lowest marginal cost of any remaining candidate once Slack ships, and it fills the cap exactly.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Include in this quarter's scope (recommended)
  ✅ Protects renewals at the accounts with the highest ARR per logo, the segment that is most expensive to replace if it churns.
  ✅ Lowest real cost of the remaining candidates: Slack-compatible webhooks mean the E1 alert payload likely ships to Mattermost with a thin adapter.
  ❌ Smallest user count of the five (3% of asks), and self-hosted deployments add support variance you cannot see from a SaaS dashboard.
B) Defer to next quarter (TODOS.md)
  ✅ Ships the quarter with two integrations and six plan-weeks, leaving slack for E3's heavy platform setup to overrun.
  ✅ Lets you confirm with account management whether any Mattermost account actually has a renewal at risk before building.
  ❌ Your highest-ARR accounts watch Slack and Teams customers get the feature first, which is the churn conversation you least want.
C) Cut entirely
  ✅ Avoids a permanent self-hosted support surface (customer-run servers, version skew, air-gapped installs).
  ✅ Keeps the roadmap to cloud-hosted platforms only, which simplifies testing and on-call.
  ❌ Tells a locked-in, high-ARR segment you will never meet them where they work; the cheapest candidate to build after Slack is a poor place to take that hit.
D) Hold — stop the chain and discuss first
  ✅ Lets you check renewal dates and ARR for the Mattermost accounts before committing the last slot.
  ✅ No disposition is recorded, so nothing has to be unwound.
  ❌ Stops the review here; the assembled-set confirmation does not fire until you say continue.
Net: you are trading the last slot for retention of your highest-ARR accounts at what is likely the cheapest build after Slack.
